input.question: why do some roller coasters exhaust their lifespan in 8-10 years while others made of the same materials last 40+ at the same parks?
input.ground_truth: Most short lived coasters tend to have significant g forces that put extra stress on the structure. This causes harder wear on the rails, substructure, and train components. If the coaster has a unique or complex mechanism (tilt coasters, original LIM, launchers, etc) it will most likely have life span issues due to those components failing more and more with age.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why do some roller coasters exhaust their lifespan in 8-10 years while others made of the same materials last 40+ at the same parks?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine roller coasters are like your favorite toy cars.

Some toy cars are played with every single day. You zoom them around, jump over things, and sometimes crash them. Because you play with them so much, they get a little broken or worn out faster.

Now, some toy cars are only played with once in a while, and you keep them in a safe spot. They don’t get banged up as much, so they last a lot longer.

Roller coasters are kind of like that. Some are really popular and lots of people ride them every day. The parts get a little tired and worn out faster, just like your toy car.

Other roller coasters might not be ridden as much, or maybe they don’t go as fast or turn as sharply. So, their parts don’t wear out as quickly, and they can last a lot longer.

Even if they’re made of the same stuff, how much they’re used and how hard they work makes a big difference!
